confirmation.summary: De novo heterozygous FGFR3 c.1138G>A on amniocentesis, confirmed at birth clinically and by newborn genetic testing.
evidence: documented a de novo heterozygous mutation of the FGFR3 gene (c.1138G>A)
The diagnosis was confirmed at birth due to typical clinical manifestations (rhizomelia, relative macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia) and genetic testing on the newborn

note.text: Before my daughter was born, scans showed that the upper parts of her legs were much shorter than expected. After she was born, her arms and legs looked short compared with the rest of her body, and the shape of her face looked different. She had trouble breathing during her first two days and needed help. Doctors later found a narrow opening at the base of her skull and a few brief pauses in breathing while she slept. She was small for her age and her muscles seemed a little floppy.
note.author: T33 hand-off (assistant-written from the article; not the parent's words)
